# Changelog

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/changelog:3.0 -->

This file records meaningful completed changes in chronological order, newest first. Current state and future work belong in `docs/repo-harness/current-state.md`.

## 2026-08-13

- Made transport-failure remediation actionable: a generated session must now check whether an alternate credential path exists and name it, preferring provider tooling used as a single-command credential helper that changes no global configuration, and handing the exact command back to the human when the remaining path needs a secret the agent cannot supply.
- Bound generated session replies to the user's stated preferred language, otherwise to the language they are writing in, and removed the hardcoded Spanish checker report literals that forced one locale regardless of the reader.
- Made documentation language a declared choice instead of a universal assumption: a repository is English-only unless it declares more locales, so a monolingual repository no longer inherits nine Spanish files, an i18n maintenance contract, and a README selector it never asked for.
- Recorded the conversation language and the declared documentation languages in the harness manifest, validated both in the generated checker, and taught congruence checking to discover them instead of being told again.
- Separated the builder's report language, which is presentation and never enters the plan digest, from the conversation language of the built harness, which is a product choice the builder asks for.

## 2026-08-12

- Fixed six bilingual review blockers: complete Spanish templates and root peers, locale-aware completeness validation, integrated localized help routing with stable digest, fail-closed reciprocal README planning, resolving documentation maps, and normative source labeling.
- Added complete English and Spanish repository and generated-harness documentation with semantic synchronization, localized routing, and single-owner operational truth.
- Localized strict builder approval domains and made apply fail closed unless both the current plan digest and exact active-language approval token validate.
- Added a lightweight pre-commit staged-scope check with behavioral coverage for exact match, extra or missing paths, status or mode changes, and pre-existing staged-work separation.
- Replaced command-by-command Git questions with intent-scoped safe-sync and commit-and-push consent, with narrow commit-only and push-only behavior plus material-change invalidation.
- Completed a blind dual review of the full builder package and recorded unresolved upgrade, approval-enforcement, runtime-set, provenance, and behavioral-test risks.
- Corrected self-hosted runtime-cache handling by separating verified on-disk parity from active-process registered skill freshness and deferring optional registered-name validation without false blocking or failure.
- Made generated Git-aware sessions actionable with scoped outcomes, mandatory concrete final questions, per-path sensitive staging review, exact commit proposals, separate push preflight, and bounded transport receipts.
- Added provider-neutral Git-aware generated session start and stop contracts with clean, dirty, no-Git, upstream, ahead, behind, and diverged handling; separate commit and push approvals; and conservative staging and publication boundaries.
- Fixed generated session-stop approvals so they resume the same close invocation, refresh post-mutation evidence, save a final continuity summary, and emit the complete handoff only after continuity succeeds.
- Expanded the product guide and generated usage guide with lifecycle, role, continuity, congruence, ownership, upgrade, and approval-boundary guidance.
- Added safe prior-version harness audits with current, stale, missing, human-evolved, and legacy classifications plus proposal-only upgrade choices.
- Added exact root pointer line detection and byte-preserving, idempotent append behavior across empty, LF, CRLF, near-match, and unrelated-content cases.
- Corrected preservation to distinguish complete empty-repository baselines from informed evolution of existing repositories, with an explicitly approved archive/start-clean alternative.
- Limited exact `APROBAR` and `DENEGAR` to the builder's content-bound apply plan; repository-shape and session choices remain conversational.
- Added the root product guide and documented canonical sources, runtime projections, and recursive self-hosting.
- Added README generation with bounded ownership markers.
- Added researched MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0-only, and custom license choice guidance.
- Added separately approved optional Git initialization and provider publication with an explicit visibility choice.
- Made generated session skills conversational outside the builder's strict digest-bound apply gate.
- Stopped versioning `.atl/`, which Gentle AI owns and regenerates.
- Aligned the builder skill frontmatter license with the repository MIT license.
- Published the repository as a private GitHub repository and pushed `main`.
- Added the MIT license.
- Split `repo-harness-builder` from `skills-pack-ld9` into its own Git repository and imported the canonical package.
- Created the minimal repository AI harness and its visible continuity documentation.
